- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast is below recent trend, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is above recent trend, adjust downward by 1–2% to avoid overbought bias.  
- Overshoots after sharp spikes (e.g., +5%+ above recent peak) should be capped at +3% to prevent overreaction.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 18-day moving average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment supports continuation.  
- For 30-day horizon, avoid over-optimism in early days (days 1–5); forecast should align with 7–10 day average unless sentiment strongly diverges.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated reversal (e.g., 2+ consecutive high/low sentiment), reduce forecast volatility by 15–20% to reflect diminishing momentum.
